## [2.13.0] - 2026-10-24

### Added
- **`hscc update --check` — the version check that never touches the
  install.** New read-only verb: queries the GitHub releases API for the
  latest tag (5 s timeout; authenticated `gh` when present, plain
  anonymous HTTPS otherwise, so public CI works), compares it to the
  `VERSION` file through the same `_get_version()` `hscc --version` uses,
  and prints the exact upgrade command for the detected install mode —
  `brew upgrade hscc` under Homebrew, `git -C <repo> pull` +
  `hscc bootstrap --yes` (script fallback named too) in a dev checkout,
  both commands when the layout is unrecognisable. NO auto-upgrade
  anywhere: the only write is the 24 h cache at
  `~/.hscc/update-check.json`. Install-mode detection prefers the
  `.hscc-brew-libexec` marker the tap drops (path-shape fallback), then a
  `.git` checkout — brew first, because a brew tree has no `.git` and
  would otherwise be told to `git pull` in a directory that is not a
  repo.
- **Cached once-a-day notices, loud/quiet per surface.** `hscc status`
  reads the cache ONLY (never fetches, can never fail) and appends one
  INFO line when the cache says newer and is ≤ 24 h old. The daemon
  piggybacks the daily check on the existing `run_heartbeat_loop` body —
  no new `PERIODIC_INTERVALS` stream — logs one WARN
  (`HSCC vX.Y.Z available (installed vA.B.C); upgrade: <cmd>`), never
  ERRORs, never raises. A failed check does not poison the cache: the
  last good answer survives on disk and the next run retries. The
  explicit verb is the only loud surface — offline or rate-limited it
  prints one short stderr line and exits 1.
- **`scripts/bump_formula.py` — the release step that bumps the Homebrew tap
  formula, so a tag lands in `pom11/homebrew-hscc` with no hand edits.**
  `Formula/hscc.rb` pins three facts about a release (archive `url`, its
  `sha256`, and the version Homebrew infers from the url) and all three used to
  be edited by hand at release time — the step that gets forgotten, after which
  the tap keeps serving the previous release while `CHANGELOG.md` and GitHub's
  `latest` say otherwise, with no symptom but a user silently installing an old
  build. `python3 scripts/bump_formula.py --tag v2.13.0` computes all three from
  the archive itself: **there is no `--sha256` flag**, because that digest is
  Homebrew's only integrity check for the tarball and a value copied from a
  release body is a value that can be wrong. The tag's version is cross-checked
  against the `VERSION` file **inside** the tarball — load-bearing, not
  belt-and-braces: the tap's `test do` asserts `hscc #{version}` against the tag
  while `hscc --version` prints the file, so a tag cut without bumping `VERSION`
  installs cleanly and then fails `brew test hscc` on every machine, and this is
  the one place that has the bytes to catch it.
  Only the release-pinned lines move: the formula's `resource` blocks pin PyPI,
  not hscc, so the rewrite asserts every changed line sits before the first
  `resource "` and that the number of `sha256` lines did not change (a formula
  shape that would swallow a PyPI digest fails loudly instead). It never *adds* a
  `version` line — the tap has none and `brew audit --strict` treats a redundant
  one as noise. `ruby -c` and the tap's vendored `address_guard.py --tracked`
  both run before the commit and restore the formula byte-for-byte if either
  rejects it; the guard is imported/shelled out to, never reimplemented, so this
  script carries no address pattern of its own. Idempotent: a current version
  exits `0` "up to date" (after re-hashing, so a stale digest is still
  corrected). Exit codes match `address_guard.py` (`2` = could not run: malformed
  tag, unreachable tarball, no ruby, no guard — never a silent pass).
  `.github/workflows/bump-homebrew-tap.yml.disabled` is the optional
  `on: release: published` transport, checked in inert: enabling it needs a
  cross-repo write token the operator creates, and it also gates on a
  `TAP_BUMP_ENABLED` repo variable so it can never paint every release red before
  that exists. No secret was created and none is enabled here.
- **`hscc bootstrap` verb + `--dry-run` + brew-libexec-aware CLI-shim skip.**
  `hscc bootstrap [flags]` locates `bootstrap.sh` relative to the resolved
  source root — repo checkout, deployed `$HERMES_HOME/plugins` copy, or a brew
  libexec tree (`<prefix>/Cellar/hscc/<ver>/libexec/hscc/`, version-stable as
  the shipped tap installs it; a versioned `libexec/hscc-<ver>/` is honoured
  too) — and execs it with every remaining argv token passed through
  (`--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--skip-*`); `HSCC_BOOTSTRAP_SH` overrides the lookup
  outright. `bootstrap.sh --dry-run` prints every planned write (plugin
  payload, CLI shim, watchdog scripts, git hooks, skills, role profiles,
  per-project orchestrators, `~/.hscc` state + serving.json, patches, config
  wiring, SOUL, review feature, trigger rules, daemon) and performs none.
  When the installer runs from a brew libexec root (marker file
  `.hscc-brew-libexec` if a tap writes one, or the `*/Cellar/*` /
  `*/libexec/hscc-*` path shapes — the shipped formula drops no marker, so
  `*/Cellar/*` is what fires on a real keg), the CLI-shim stage is SKIPPED
  with the reason printed — brew already owns `hscc` on PATH, and a shim
  into the Hermes venv would shadow it with a second, brew-invisible entry
  point.
  Non-brew trees keep the previous behaviour byte-for-byte. `hscc_cli`'s own
  `hscc_daemon` lookup gained a brew-libexec leg (ancestor `libexec/hscc` and
  `libexec/hscc-*` dirs, newest first, checked before `~/.hermes/plugins`) so
  a brew-installed `hscc` is self-contained: its venv lives inside
  `libexec/`, where the old sibling/repo candidates never saw the payload.

### Changed
- **README install story is brew-first.** `brew tap pom11/hscc && brew
  install hscc` followed by `hscc bootstrap --yes` is now THE quick start;
  the `git clone` + `bootstrap.sh` flow is relabelled "Install from source
  (development)" and is where a contributor goes, not where a user goes. The
  division of labour is stated where a reader will hit it: `brew install`
  stays inside its own keg and writes nothing into `~/.hermes` or `~/.hscc`,
  and `hscc bootstrap` is the step that does (with the CLI-shim stage skipped
  on a keg, because brew owns `hscc` on PATH), including the fallback the
  formula's own caveats print for a keg that predates the `bootstrap` verb.
  New **Upgrade** table — `brew upgrade hscc` + re-bootstrap vs `git pull` +
  re-bootstrap — and a new **Check whether you are behind** section
  documenting `hscc update --check` from the merged implementation: the quiet
  up-to-date one-liner, the `installed:` / `latest:` / `upgrade:` block, the
  one-line stderr + exit 1 offline behaviour, the 24 h cache at

  release: `up to date` is treated as a claim about the PUBLIC tap, so it is only
  made after the checkout has been synced onto origin and found to carry no
  unpushed commit — an unpushed bump commit is *published* (`status: bumped`,
  `recovered_push: true`) instead of being reported as fine, and with `--no-push`
  the run refuses rather than green-lighting a release the tap does not serve; the
  recovery push runs `ruby -c` and the guard over the committed tree first, because
  that commit was written by someone else and has never been through them; a
  pin that exists only as an uncommitted hand edit is refused, not committed as
  the tool's own work; a checkout that has diverged is refused, never rebased
  into public history; unpushed commits touching files besides the formula stop a
  push, because publishing an operator's private tap work to a public repo is a
  disclosure decision, not a release step; and a `git`/`ruby`/guard step that
  hangs surfaces as `CannotRun` (rc=2) naming the hung step, not a traceback.

- **`hscc cluster up` hung "forever" on an already-serving unit and starved
  the rest of the fleet.** The 2026-10-22 cooldown repro: a unit that already
  answered `/v1/models` 200 kept its `sparkrun run --no-follow --ensure` call
  open for 19 min (then 8 min on retry) while the SERIAL plan loop waited, so
  the other two units never launched. Three fixes in `cmd_cluster_up`:
  (1) each launch is bounded by a dedicated LAUNCH-PHASE timeout —
  `HSCC_CLUSTER_UP_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT`, default **180s**, deliberately NOT the
  1200s model-load grace — and an expiry is reported as that unit failing
  with the captured output tail, not swallowed; (2) a unit whose every span
  node already answers `/v1/models` with a parseable NON-EMPTY catalogue is
  reported already-up and sparkrun is never invoked (fail-open probe: any
  error = launch anyway, `--ensure` makes that safe); (3) launches run
  CONCURRENTLY over the independent hosts (ThreadPoolExecutor) while the
  per-unit report stays plan-ordered, and the A2 guard keeps its single
  prefetched status fetch. Sparkrun-side attribution (fix 4, source-read
  only, no hscc workaround): the hang is sparkrun's OWN readiness wait — in
  v0.4.1 `--ensure` "still wait[s] for readiness" and `--no-follow` only
  stops the log stream; `wait_for_run` blocks until the startup probe sees a
  first non-empty inference TOKEN, which a model that loads far past the
  port-bind can take ~66 min to deliver while `/v1/models` already answers
  200 — the operator's own hand-run log shows exactly that shape
  (`Waiting for server readiness... startup observation exceeded its
  deadline ... total 3947.3s`). The local `ssh ... bash -s` observation is
  that wait's per-poll SSH probe, not a missing-EOF bug: every `bash -s`
  site in sparkrun provably closes its stdin (`input=` or `communicate`).
  `--no-ready-wait` is the sparkrun-side flag that skips the wait; hscc
  deliberately does NOT pass it (the hscc launch timeout bounds the whole
  call instead, which also covers a genuinely wedged ssh).
- **`hscc_daemon.serving.resolve_cluster_config()`'s fallback could exec the
  operator's live sparkrun CLI — and on this host it DID, three times per
  daemon suite run.** The call was
  `subprocess.run("timeout 2 sparkrun cluster list --json", shell=True, ...)`:
  a shell string cannot be argv-rewritten by `sparkrun_bin.exec_argv`, so the
  `HSCC_SPARKRUN_BIN` hermetic pin never covered it (the daemon conftest's own
  docstring recorded exactly this gap). Now a LIST argv built by
  `sparkrun_bin.argv` — the repo's single execution chokepoint — with
  `shell=True` dropped and `timeout=3` replacing the PATH-dependent
  `timeout 2` wrapper (macOS keeps `timeout` in Homebrew). Pinned by
  `hscc_daemon/tests/test_serving_fallback_no_live_cli.py` against a fake CLI
  on a PATH-less HOME.

### Security
- **sparkrun argv FENCE at the conftest level (stop-work order; live `:4000`
  proxy SIGTERM incident).** One shared harness,
  `hscc-cluster/tests/sparkrun_fence.py`, wired into the four suites that can
  reach the CLI (`hscc-cluster`, `hscc-commands`, `hscc_daemon`,
  `sparkrun-hermes`): it wraps every subprocess entrypoint, resolves each
  argv element against PATH, and BLOCKS + FAILS the test whose call resolves
  to the operator's real sparkrun CLI (bare `sparkrun`, an absolute CLI path
  outside a pytest per-test tmp dir, a CLI at any LATER argv element, or the
  CLI name embedded in a `shell=True` string). Recipe paths named
  `sparkrun.yaml` are pinned as NOT CLI tokens (false-positive guard), and the
  sanctioned escape hatches are a `tmp_path` fake or an explicit
  expect-block — the fence reports blocked-vs-unexpected in the terminal
  summary every run. First run of the fence caught **six** real leak sites
  that had been silently exec'ing the operator's CLI in CI-shaped runs:
  `_pin_topology`'s `monkeypatch.setattr` reading lazy `clusterlib.HEAD/NODES/
  NAS_HOST` (→ live `sparkrun cluster list --json` for EVERY cluster test),
  a live discovery-cache WRITE from `test_discovery`, real `sparkrun show`
  per shipped recipe in `test_template_intent` (now opt-in gated), and the
  three `resolve_cluster_config` fallback shells above. Conftests now pin
  canned discovery output instead; no normal test run touches the fleet.

## [2.11.0] - 2026-10-19

### Added
- **dep-bump fork-branch guard**: the runtime dep-bump flow now knows sparkrun
  runs from OUR FORK BRANCH. Canonical rule in `hscc_daemon/dep_bump_guard.py`
  (branch `feat/proxy-least-in-flight`, remote `pom11/sparkrun`): a sparkrun
  bump REBASES the fork branch onto the new upstream tag and keeps it checked
  out — never `git checkout main`, never reinstall from upstream (either one
  silently drops the proxy `router_settings` passthrough and the
  least-in-flight balancer). The rule is injected into the CI-generated bump
  PR body (`.github/scripts/check_runtime_deps.py`) and the dep-watcher
  verification card (`scripts/dep_pr_watcher.py`) for sparkrun bumps only, and
  into the runtime-bump skill (`references/runtime-bump-verification.md`).
- **verify check `proxy_router_settings`** + `hscc_daemon/proxy_router.py`:
  pure-read comparison of `~/.config/sparkrun/proxy.yaml` (router_settings +
  gateways.litellm.balancing) against the live
  `~/.cache/sparkrun/proxy/litellm_config.yaml`. WARN-only (never fails,
  never writes, never restarts); flags divergence, a requested balancer absent
  from litellm_settings.callbacks, non-mapping router_settings, unimplemented
  balancing values, and the `routing_strategy: least-busy` trap (no-op on the
  pinned LiteLLM — the working knob is `gateways.litellm.balancing:
  least-in-flight`).
- **proxy stream carries the drift verdict**: the daemon `proxy` stream
  records `router_drift` / `router_drift_warn` on both the healthy and the
  unhealthy state writes and logs a WARN while drift is live — a proxy can
  serve every alias yet route blind after a bump dropped the fork branch.
- **HSCCUITests target (the app's first).** Four tests drive the operator's
  exact walks with real taps, fixture-fed (HSCC_DEBUG_FIXTURES), launched
  straight into the drawer via the DEBUG-only HSCC_DEBUG_OPEN_DRAWER seam.
  RED on 2.9.0 (commit A), GREEN on the fix (commit B), `xcodebuild test
  -scheme HSCCUITests` on the iPhone 16 simulator.
- **iOS nav-graph walker gate (`ios-app/scripts/nav_graph_check.sh` + `UITests/NavGraphUITests.swift`).** A screen that renders is not a screen you can leave. The walker walks EVERY drawer screen the way a user does and fails naming the screen + missing edge (`DEAD END [screen]: …`): drawer → every row → screen marker → back → same-row re-tap (the 2.9.0 regression) for all 17 drawer destinations; one level in where detail exists (projects → project → chat/board/settings, cards → card detail) with each back asserted against its predecessor; pull-to-refresh as a REAL gesture (a slow coordinate drag — `swipeDown()` never fires `.refreshable` on iOS 26, proven) whose receipt is the app's live served-count AX probe incrementing, with the badge pollers silenced for the walk so the increment can only be the refresh; honest EMPTY (`HSCC_DEBUG_FIXTURE_DIR=empty`) and ERROR (`HSCC_DEBUG_FIXTURE_FAIL=1`, every GET answers the API error contract) states that must still be navigable; and a disconnected pass (`HSCC_DEBUG_OFFLINE=1`) where the whole drawer must still round-trip without any fixtures. The screen list is code-derived — `scripts/nav_graph_screens.py` parses AppShell/Sidebar and a drawer row without a walk plan breaks the gate before the walker even runs (`NavGraphScreenTable.swift` is the committed generated table; `check` fails on drift). The negative self-check (`HSCC_NEGATE_BACK=1` removes the drawer's open/close affordances, passed into the test-runner process via xcodebuild's `TEST_RUNNER_` passthrough) requires the walk to go RED, and `testNegativeSeamEngages` guards that wiring from inside the suite (`SEAM INERT` names the harness, not the walker): a walker that cannot fail is not a gate. All seams are `#if DEBUG`, default-off, zero release-path change; fixtures still never touch the network (`fixtures.invalid`, RFC 6761). What the walker proves vs what it does NOT prove (pixel correctness) is written up in `docs/design/NAV_GRAPH_t_810ab152.md`. First full walk already earned its keep: it found t_706129d8 — back from a project's Chat/Board/Settings pops PAST the overview (the overview is pushed by a value-less NavigationLink while sub-pages append to the bound path), asserted as an expected failure until that card lands, plus two fixture-mode client gaps (card detail + diff) fixed here.
- **`verify.provider_routing` guard.** While the applied template is
  `uniform_pool` (flag now recorded in `~/.hscc/applied_template.json` at
  apply), any fleet-node host in a `base_url`/fallback url anywhere in the
  root `~/.hermes/config.yaml` or a profile config is a FAIL. Loopback proxy
  URLs pass on any port; non-uniform templates skip (direct is legitimate);
  missing state or an unresolvable fleet-node set is UNVERIFIED, never a
  silent pass. The node set comes from sparkrun's own `resolve_hosts` under
  sparkrun's venv python — pure-read, no template parsing, no ssh.
- **Hermetic gate `scripts/connection_probe_check.sh`.** Compiles
  `ConnectionMonitor.swift` verbatim + the committed live `/v1/health`
  capture, 23 assertions (endpoint pinned to /v1/health, decode contract,
  classification table, first-probe flip, no-pin after both failure kinds,
  cluster-switch reset), no socket opened; `CONNECTION_PROBE_NEGATIVE_TEST=1`
  proves it can fail. `connection_banner_check.sh` unchanged in logic
  (APIError.swift joined its verbatim compile for the probe's typed catch).

### Changed
- **2.10.0 was re-cut from `528bad41` instead of `baf98413`.** The first
  release branch (`release/2.10.0` @ `73da1eff`, PR #41) was cut before
  PR #43 landed, so its materialised changelog lacked the
  `dispatcher_wedge` benign-hold watchdog entry — the very fix 2.10.0 was
  gated on. This branch (`release/2.10.0-v2`) re-runs
  `scripts/changelog_fragments.py release --version 2.10.0` on the current
  main: the released section is PR #41's 27 entries verbatim plus the
  `t_160d306f` watchdog entry, and the consumed fragments move to
  `changelog.d/archive/2.10.0/`. PR #41 is closed as superseded; its branch
  is untouched (no force-push). No code changed in the re-cut — changelog,
  VERSION, and fragment archival only.

### Fixed
- **A review card nobody could spawn restarted the gateway every 30 minutes.** `dispatcher_wedge` counted a `status=review` row as *spawnable* even when the running Hermes has no review lane to spawn it into, so the detector declared a "GENUINE STALL" that no dispatcher action could ever clear and the recovery restarted the gateway on every cooldown expiry — four gateway SIGTERMs in two hours on a card whose work had already merged. Three doors let that happen and all are now shut: the raw-SQL fallback in `_board_snapshot` counted any `status='review'` row whenever the kanban lib exposes no `has_spawnable_review`; the lib-predicate path ORed `has_spawnable_review` in unconditionally, even with `kanban.review_dispatch` off; and the per-profile room check asked whether any assignee with unclaimed *ready or review* work was under its cap, so a parked review row owned by an idle profile manufactured room for a board whose ready-holding profile was correctly at its per-profile cap. Review work now counts as spawnable — and now answers the room question — only when the runtime can actually dispatch it: the lib exposes `has_spawnable_review` **and** the dispatcher's own `review_dispatch_enabled()` gate is not off (that function is called, not reimplemented, so the answer cannot drift from the dispatcher's; `kanban.auto_review` is the review-*pairing* policy and is deliberately not consulted). Non-dispatchable review cards are reported separately as `stale_review` + `review_count` on the `dispatcher` stream with one WARNING daemon-log line per cooldown window — "N review cards not dispatchable by this runtime" — and never flip the stream red, never mutate the recovery state, never restart anything. Recovery also gained a per-incident restart latch: every restart records the stall's spawnable/roomy `signature` and whether the runtime could dispatch it, and a stall the runtime cannot dispatch is never restarted twice — a green tick in between renews the attempt budget (A1's behaviour, kept for dispatcher-fixable wedges) but no longer re-arms a restart for a stall that was already paid for. Verified RED-first: on the pre-fix source one `review` row against a lib without the helper produced `spawnable=['default']`, a red stream and 4 restarts across cooldowns with green ticks between, and a capped-profile board looked roomy because of a review row; after the fix the same boards stay green and restart zero times. Every gate was mutation-tested in isolation (11 mutants — including a removed call site and a faithful re-introduction of the old conflation): all 11 are caught by the suite, with the source restored byte-identical after each.
- **`install_dep_watcher.sh` wrote the poller to a dir the cron job could
  never read.** Hermes resolves a bare `--script NAME` only against the bound
  home's `scripts/` dir (`$HERMES_HOME/scripts`; profiles never share files),
  but the installer hard-coded the shared `~/.hermes/scripts/` while
  `hermes cron create` bound the invoking profile's home. Installing from a
  profile shell therefore produced a job whose script could not be found —
  `hscc-dep-watcher` failed 17 consecutive daily runs under the
  backend-engineer profile. The zombie job was removed with
  `hermes cron remove`; the shared-home job (the installer's real target all
  along) had been running green daily the whole time, so no verification card
  was ever actually owed one: no `needs-cluster-check` PR was open at any run
  boundary while that job was live. The installer now derives
  `HERMES_SCRIPTS` from the same `$HERMES_HOME` the cron CLI binds, and
  `scripts/tests/test_install_dep_watcher.py` pins the invariant
  (install/uninstall resolve to one home; no hard-coded shared path;
  byte-identical copy).
- **The 5-min proxy relaunch loop could no-op for hours in silence.**
  On 2026-10-18 `:4000` refused connections for 3h09m while the daemon ran
  ~36 plain `sparkrun proxy start` attempts, each logging one WARN and
  discarding the command's "already running (PID …)" output. Root cause is
  sparkrun-side (restart SIGTERMs only the state-file wrapper PID; the real
  litellm socket owner orphaned on the port, and the replacement wrapper
  stayed alive without ever binding, so `is_running()` read "running"
  forever — full evidence and upstream asks in
  `docs/audits/PROXY_RELAUNCH_NOOP_2026-10-18.md`). hscc-side hardening:
  every failed relaunch/repair now logs ERROR with the folded command
  output; a durable consecutive-failure streak (`relaunch_streak` in the
  proxy state file — survives daemon restart; cooldown/lease/breaker-deferred
  ticks attempt nothing and never count) escalates at
  `HSCC_PROXY_RELAUNCH_MAX_CONSECUTIVE` (default 3) stalled attempts to the
  proven stop → cmdline-vetted reap of the HOLLOW tracked PID → plain start
  → port-owner-verified repair (foreign-cmdline PIDs are refused, and
  `--restart` is never invoked on the escalation path); one throttled
  high-priority desktop notify + `proxy.relaunch.stalled` events row per
  `HSCC_PROXY_STALL_NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_S`, never during an intentional-autodown
  window; repair verification polls while the port is unbound instead of
  trusting a single immediate owner check (the 01:41:42 "UNVERIFIED — port
  owner None" line was a race with litellm's slow bind). Exit code is not
  success: rc-0 over an empty catalogue no longer defuses the streak.
  11 red-on-old tests in `TestProxyRelaunchStall` (11/11 fail with the fix
  stashed), mutation-probed 7/7.
- **`hscc cluster up --help` / `hscc cluster down --help` printed "unknown
  argument" (rc=1) instead of help** (operator's final pass on PR #33; audit
  rows D-rc owner=F3 in scripts/tests/cli_help_expected.json). Help now wins
  over the F6 refusal for an explicit help token: both verbs route through the
  `_CLUSTER_SUBCOMMAND_HELP` shape (the cb352d40 lane shape — usage line,
  options, read-only/destructive marker) and exit 0. The refusal itself is
  byte-identical and still fires for `up`/`down` with any NON-help unknown
  token (`up --force`, `down --now`) — that is where the F6 incident guard
  lives now, and the probe token moved from `--help` to `--foo` accordingly.
  `cluster -h`/`--help` (group help) and `hscc profiles -h`/`--help` (was
  loading the cluster engine and RENDERING PROFILES instead of printing help)
  got the same treatment.
- **`hscc escalate -h` and `hscc autoscale -h` RAN the read-only verb instead
  of printing help** (operator-verbatim: "run the read-only command instead of
  printing help"). The daemon-verb branch matched only `args[1] == "--help"`,
  so the short flag fell through to dispatch. The branch now uses a
  raw-tail help-token scan: any `-h`/`--help` anywhere in the verb's tail
  prints the COMMAND_HELP entry rc=0 before dispatch. Same shape applied to
  the advanced-command branch and the profiles handler.
- **The audit gate probed `--help` only, so every `-h` path on the CLI was
  unmeasured** (F5's recorded gap in docs/audits/NOTES_t_fc307a51.md; worst
  case `start-daemon -h` LAUNCHES the daemon loop). The oracle now probes
  `-h` alongside `--help` on every flag-kind surface, and a new **D-h**
  check fails any surface whose `-h` output differs from its `--help` output
  (the "did `-h` actually print help" test). Launch-class verbs (`start`,
  `stop`, `install`, `uninstall`, `start-daemon`, `heal`) are exempt from the
  live `-h` probe but the exemption is VISIBLE (recorded in report skips and
  pinned by test), and their inertness is proven in-process instead:
  `hscc_daemon/tests/test_cli_h_shortflag.py`, 122 cases, landmine-raises on
  the daemon-loop entry, the mutating verbs, and `ClusterEngine` methods.
  `start-daemon -h` cannot launch the loop — the landmine fires first.
  Probe count 178 → 299 (153 paths); MIN_PROBES raised in the same commit
  with zero slack.
- **iOS drawer dead-end: opening the HSCC sidebar no longer traps you.** On
  iPhone (compact width, verified on iPhone 16 / iOS 26.3) opening the drawer
  (the "HSCC" Work/Cluster page) left NO way back — no close, no back, swipe
  didn't dismiss, and tapping a row (even the already-selected Home row)
  never left it. Root cause, proven with the app's new XCUITest target before
  any fix shipped: once the system presents the compact NavigationSplitView
  sidebar column it exposes zero dismiss affordances, row activation never
  switches columns (`List(selection:)` doesn't even write the binding on a
  same-value re-tap), and both documented column controls
  (`preferredCompactColumn`, `columnVisibility`) are inert from the app side
  in both directions on this OS. The shell now owns the drawer outright: a
  slide-over panel over the one app-wide stack, with an explicit `Menu`
  (sidebar.left) entry on every screen's nav bar, an X close button +
  tap-outside scrim on the panel, and row activation that ALWAYS leaves the
  drawer — same-row re-tap included. Home hero/tiles/dock, deep links and
  requestedTab routing are untouched; `go()` keeps its stack/alias rules.
- **Back from a project's Chat/Board/Settings lands on the overview again.**
  Drawer → Projects → a project → Chat (or Board, or Settings) → the nav-bar
  back skipped the project Overview and landed on the Projects list. The walker
  (t_810ab152) found it; AX-verified for all three sub-pages.

Cause: `ProjectsView` pushed `ProjectDetailView` with a VALUE-LESS
`NavigationLink`, so the Overview never entered `router.projectsPath`. Every
sub-page pushes onto that same bound path (Chat via `openSection`'s append,
Board/Settings via their `NavigationLink(value:)` rows); when SwiftUI's
`NavigationStack` gets an append on a bound path it rewrites the path and drops
the off-path value-less view — so the sub-page's predecessor became the Projects
list (the back button was even labelled "Projects").

Fix: both project rows (live + stale list) now push
`ProjectRoute.projectDetail(name:board:)` — the route `AppShell.projectRouteView`
ALREADY registers and `DeepLinkRouter` already builds `hscc://` paths from. User
taps and deep links take one path, so every pop lands 1:1, and
`ProjectDetailView`'s pending-segment guard (written against `.projectDetail`
being the path's last entry) is live for real taps for the first time.

Tests: the walker's `knownBugBackThenOverview` tripwire (XCTExpectFailure + the
`ensureOnOverview` recovery path) is deleted; chat/board/settings backs are
plain predecessor-return assertions. RED on the old code (3 failures: the pop
landed on the Projects list), GREEN after the fix — back label "hscc" on all
three. Full nav-graph gate green incl. the negative self-check.
- **`test_live_hscc_autodown_unchanged_by_suite` raced the live daemon's
  30s autodown heartbeat.** The guard byte-hashed the real
  `~/.hscc/autodown.json` before/after a sandboxed re-run of its module,
  but `run_autodown_loop` (interval=30s) rewrites that file every tick via
  `record_activity()`/`save_config()` — advancing `last_activity_iso`/
  `wake_source` — so any tick landing inside the read window failed the
  byte-identical assert false-positive (observed in the 2026-10-18
  merged-tree sweep; measured: the file's md5 changes within 33s on a live
  host). Replaced with the design the daemon-side `test_no_live_hscc_leak`
  already documents for exactly this reason: a planted-sandbox check (the
  module re-runs against a fake HOME holding a static seeded autodown.json —
  deterministic, no live file involved) plus a semantic live check on only
  the operator-decision keys (`enabled`, `idle_minutes`), which the tick can
  never rewrite. The nested run also gets `HSCC_DIR` stripped (it outranks
  HOME in `ensure_autodown`'s path resolution — an exported value would
  punch through the fake HOME), and `test_main_prints_json` delvars it for
  the same reason.
- **A non-spawnable assignee on a ready card silenced the dispatcher watchdog
  instead of paging.** The PR #43 L2 board gate
  (`board_state_explains_stall()` in `hscc_daemon/dispatcher_wedge.py`) counted a
  ready card whose assignee names no Hermes profile as an EXPLAINED hold, so the
  watchdog suppressed the restart **and went quiet** — on exactly the silent
  no-dispatch failure mode the fleet has been bitten by before (the dispatcher
  drops unknown assignees and the card sits in `ready` forever). Suppressing the
  restart was correct: `launchctl kickstart` has never once fixed a typo'd
  profile name. Silence was not. The gate now reports those cards structurally
  (`GateVerdict.nonspawnable` — still a `(explained, detail)` 2-tuple, so every
  existing caller and injected fake is unchanged) and
  `recover_dispatcher_wedge()` fires the DISTINCT operator notification for that
  class — card id, board, assignee string, `no worker will ever run it`, and that
  NO restart was attempted — under the existing 1/h hold-notify throttle and the
  existing desktop channel (title `HSCC Dispatcher: unrunnable ready card`),
  reporting `reason: nonspawnable_assignee`. A board mixing a cap-held card with
  a typo'd one notifies about the typo'd card only, and still never restarts.
  Non-spawnability stays defined in exactly one place
  (`_assignee_is_nonspawnable()`, the dispatcher's own `skipped_nonspawnable`
  bucket); a profile lookup that cannot decide still means "assume spawnable",
  so the restart path is unchanged — fail closed.
- **`template apply` re-infected direct node URLs into hermes config under
  `uniform_pool`.** The top-level `model` block was correctly aimed at the
  family proxy, yet the `custom` provider still got
  `base_url = http://<node>:<port>/v1` and `model.default = <node>:<port>` on
  every apply — bypassing the proxy hermes is supposed to be the only chat
  route through, and dying with the pinned node. Under `uniform_pool` (with a
  family proxy owning the worker port) `custom` now carries the same proxy
  URL (`chat_url`) and the same probe-resolved alias as the model block —
  never a second URL, never an id the endpoint does not serve; a carried
  `host:port`-shaped default is dropped rather than kept. Non-uniform plans
  keep the historical direct-node entry byte-for-byte.
- **`family-*` providers got `localhost:<port>` as `model.default`** — a
  host:port no endpoint resolves as a model. They now carry the family's
  role alias (`worker-model`, via `_unit_alias`), the name the family proxy
  actually answers to.
- **PipelineWatchdog's vLLM auto-restart could race an in-flight heal and
  launch a hollow duplicate of a cluster-up-owned unit.** The
  2026-10-18 01:38 UTC incident (redacted timeline kept as a test fixture):
  engine-wedge recovery held the heal lease while it stopped `orch` and
  relaunched it via `hscc cluster up`; the proxy stream honoured the lease
  and deferred at 01:38:34; 10s later the watchdog ignored the same lease,
  issued a target-less stop (sparkrun: "Error: Must specify TARGET or
  --all" — a no-op the code logged and continued past), and launched a
  SECOND job from the bare recipe whose vllm never started (:8000 was
  already held) — then logged `#270: success`. The hollow container sat
  ~7h. Four gates now hold: (1) `pipeline_watchdog` consults
  `heal_lease.read_lease()` BEFORE any attempt (the same deferral machinery
  the proxy WARN used — no second lock) and does nothing but log + state the
  deferral while held; `restart_vllm` re-checks for its other caller
  (trigger.py); (2) a (node,port) registered in serving.json is
  `hscc cluster up`'s exclusive launch surface — a watchdog-initiated
  restart there is REFUSED with a WARN naming the unit; (3) the stop is
  `sparkrun stop <recipe> --hosts <node>` (new `serving.vllm_stop_cmd`;
  `--all` is never a fallback; no resolvable TARGET ⇒ abort without ever
  issuing the broken argv) and a failed stop ABORTS before any launch;
  (4) `ok` requires the launched unit to actually serve — the engine-wedge
  streaming probe (`health._probe_unit_generation`) gates the lifetime
  counter, the `#N: success` log and the load-grace window, and a streak of
  unverified launches (`WATCHDOG_VERIFY_ALARM_AFTER`) escalates a critical
  NOT-SERVING notification. The stop→verify window itself runs under the
  lease as `vllm-auto-restart` so the other repair paths back off it.
- **A parked review row could reconcile a benign-hold claim it was never part of (rebase interaction of PR #35 x PR #43).** Rebasing PR #35's review-row spawnability work onto the landed benign-hold logic surfaced a combined case neither branch tested alone: PR #43's layer-1 reconciliation asks whether the dispatcher's `Last tick held back: active_pr=N` claim is backed by `N` pending rows, and its pending counter counted `ready + review` rows unconditionally. On a runtime with **no review lane** — exactly the class of runtime PR #35 exists for — the dispatcher's own tick never even enumerates review rows (`review_dispatch_enabled()` off short-circuits `_lane_rows(conn, "review")` before the clause is built), so its hold claim can never be counting a parked review card. Yet one such card padded the pending count and reconciled a claim the dispatcher could not have made, silently exempting a live wedge from detection for up to the 900 s lookback. The pending count now follows the same capability answer the spawnable decision uses (`review_capable` from `_review_dispatch_capable`), mirroring `include_review=review_capable` in the room check: review rows count when this runtime can dispatch the lane, and never when it cannot. Fail-open direction of the capability probe is unchanged; when the lane is dispatchable, a genuinely held review card still reconciles exactly as PR #43 shipped. Also pinned the layer-2 board-state gate from the other side with regression tests: it enumerates `ready` cards via the sanctioned CLI only, consults only boards the probe declared spawnable, and can therefore never let a parked review row "explain" a genuine ready wedge. Proven RED-first (three combined-case tests fail on the pre-rebase-interaction source) and mutation-tested (9 mutants across both layers — pre-fix pending count, always-ready-only pending, inverted capability, gate listing review rows, gate consulting stale-review boards, disabled restart latch, disabled hold exemption, re-ORed review spawnable, room check ignoring capability — all 9 killed, source restored byte-identical after each).
- **`install_escalate_watcher.sh` had the same profile/scripts-dir drift fixed
  for the dep-watcher in t_3aadd2c0.** Hermes resolves a bare `--script NAME`
  only against the bound home's `scripts/` dir (`$HERMES_HOME/scripts`;
  profiles never share files), but the installer hard-coded the shared
  `~/.hermes/scripts/` while `hermes cron create` binds the invoking profile's
  home — running it from a profile shell would produce an
  `hscc-escalate-watcher` job whose script can never be found. The installer
  now derives `HERMES_SCRIPTS` from the same `$HERMES_HOME` the cron CLI binds,
  and `scripts/tests/test_install_escalate_watcher.py` pins the invariant
  (install/uninstall resolve to one home; no hard-coded shared path;
  byte-identical copy). Operator-side: the live shared-home job
  `6407ea32e1dd` had its stale `--deliver telegram` (telegram dropped
  fleet-wide in 6ac173c6) re-pointed to `local` via `hermes cron edit`; the
  runner already self-notifies via `hscc_daemon.desktop`, and the job's
  schedule and script were left untouched.
- **The drawer's connection pill no longer says "checking…" forever.** With
  the API up, the drawer's server pill (and Home's hero) sat on
  "checking…" / "unknown" indefinitely. `ConnectionMonitor.status` changed
  only via `requestSucceeded()`/`requestFailed()` from completed `HSCCClient`
  requests — and the drawer makes no request of its own, so nothing ever
  resolved `.unknown`. (The old launch ping had been deleted for a different
  reason — a one-shot cold-start FAILURE pinned the banner — which never
  licensed an eternal `.unknown`.) The monitor keeps its passive contract and
  gains the missing active half: while the drawer header is visible and the
  app is configured, a `.task` keyed on `connectionIdentity` runs one cheap
  authed `GET /v1/health` immediately, then re-checks every 15 s (30 s
  back-off when the server refuses the credential), and stops with zero
  traffic when the drawer closes (task cancellation on disappear). The first
  real result — probe or request — flips `.unknown`; the dot then tracks the
  most recent outcome while visible. A failed probe never pins the banner:
  the loop keeps observing and any real success clears it (the t_4889e978
  contract). `!isConfigured` fires nothing — first-run still reads "not
  configured". Auth refusal (401/403/`unauthorized`) is surfaced honestly as
  unreachable with a token-specific reason ("check it in Settings"), not a
  Tailscale guess; any other HTTP response still proves reachability
  (any-response contract). Full state machine documented on
  `ConnectionMonitor`; probe logic is a pure, injected-call
  `ConnectionProbe` enum so it is fully gate-covered.

  top-level verb × `-h`/`--help` in-process with the daemon loop, mutating

  no HOME writes; positive controls that the read-only verbs still RUN
  without a help token), plus re-pinned
  `hscc_daemon/tests/test_cluster_cli_help.py` (up/down help prints, rc 0,

## [2.10.0] - 2026-10-17

### Added
- **CLI help-surface gate.** `scripts/tests/test_cli_help_surface.py`
  (+ engine `scripts/hscc_cli_help_audit.py`, expectations
  `scripts/tests/cli_help_expected.json`) walks the code-derived command
  surface — 153 paths, 182 sandboxed help probes at widths 80/120/500,
  75 examples parse-checked — and asserts the operator's five invariants:
  no standalone `flightdeck` in rendered help, no continuation-less wraps,
  every `example:` line parses through the real parser (never executed),
  `--help` executes nothing (sandboxed HOME + recording sparkrun/hermes/gh/git
  canaries + LaunchAgent/port tripwires), and each surface's help style is
  recorded for the convergence card. Today's violations ship as 326 named
  expectation rules keyed to fix cards F1–F5 (`t_7b0f65c8` findings doc);
  fixing one without pruning its rule goes red as STALE, any new violation
  goes red as NEW — both directions mutation-tested.

### Changed
- **`docs/audits/artifacts/CLI_HELP_FINDINGS.json` is no longer committed**
  (PR #33 review follow-up decision, recorded in
  `docs/audits/PR33-FOLLOWUPS-t_36580090.md`). It is the raw output of
  `audit()` — a pure function of the tree — and every fix card pruning
  findings silently rotted the snapshot (326 findings at audit time; the
  rules file is at 56 after F1/BROKEN-* landed). Nothing reads the
  committed copy. Regenerate on demand:
  `HSCC_CLI_HELP_WRITE_ARTIFACT=1 pytest scripts/tests/test_cli_help_surface.py -k artifact`
  or `python scripts/hscc_cli_help_audit.py --json <path>`. The path is
  gitignored; the human-authored findings doc
  (`docs/audits/CLI_HELP_2026-10-15.md`) remains committed.

### Fixed
- **The dispatcher-wedge watchdog restarted the gateway for BENIGN
  dispatcher holds (safety-ops, 2026-10-17).** A card held back by the
  dispatcher's own respawn guard — `Last tick held back: active_pr=1.` — is
  the dispatcher working as designed, but the watchdog read the red
  "kanban dispatcher stuck" warning plus the spawnable-ready predicate as a
  genuine stall and kicked `launchctl kickstart` three times in 65 minutes
  (12:13, 12:43, 13:17) while the tick ladder climbed 6→11→16→21→26. Held
  is not wedged. Two fail-closed layers now guard the restart:
  (1) `classify_dispatcher_hold()` parses the warning's hold payload from
  the gateway log (fresh lookback only) and, when every hold name is in the
  vocabulary mirrored from Hermes' `describe_suppression` — `active_pr`,
  `recent_success`, `rate_limited`, `skipped_locked`, `memory_pressure` —
  and the claimed counts reconcile against the boards' pending queue, the
  zero-spawn tick is explained and never declared; (2) before any restart,
  `board_state_explains_stall()` consults the sanctioned `hermes kanban
  list/show --json` and suppresses (log + operator notify, with the reason)
  when every ready card is explainably held (fleet cap, per-profile cap,
  fresh benign `respawn_guarded` event, rate-limited release). `blocker_auth`,
  unknown reason names, a missing clause, a stale warning, an unreconcilable
  claim or an unreadable board all stay wedge-worthy — a true wedge (ready
  queue non-empty, zero spawns, NO benign explanation) still restarts, proven
  by replaying the verbatim incident ladder both ways
  (`tests/fixtures/gateway_wedge_incident_20261017.log`, mutation-probed in
  both directions). Upstream report for the warning itself counting benign
  holds: `docs/audits/DISPATCHER_HOLD_UPSTREAM_2026-10-17.md`.
- **Four `project` verbs were still doubling the group name.** The
  `hscc project <verb>` alias (1.16.0) shipped with a hand-maintained verb
  table that drifted: `sessions`, `digest`, `link` and `unlink` were added
  to flightdeck's `project` subgroup and never added to
  `_PROJECT_SUBGROUP_VERBS`, so exactly those four kept reading the awkward
  `hscc project project <verb>` (the doubled form always works — the alias
  only upgrades the short form). The table now covers the whole subgroup,
  and pins in `hscc_daemon/tests/test_hscc_cli.py` fail listing the
  drifters if it ever lags the parser again (and if it ever claims a verb
  the subgroup lacks, or one that shadows a top-level command).
- **Help stopped teaching the doubled form.** All 15 `example: hscc project
  project …` epilogs (project.py, sync.py) and the hscc-project README now
  advertise the short form the alias actually supports; the doubled
  invocation keeps working (parse and behaviour unchanged, pinned per verb
  by test). The inner subgroup parser now pins `prog="hscc project"` so its
  rendered usage lines read `usage: hscc project link …`, not the doubled
  form. The audit's parse oracle models the daemon's alias promotion the
  same way `_handle_project` implements it (set membership +
  top-level-wins guard), so the documented short form parses — F1 had
  called the doubled form "canonical" only because the oracle rejected the
  short one.
- **`hscc autodown <sub> --help` executed the verb instead of printing
  help** (audit BROKEN B7/B8/B9). `cmd_autodown` had a group-level `--help`
  branch but none per subcommand, so `disable --help` DISARMED autodown
  (rewrote `~/.hscc/autodown.json` + `watchdog-block.json`), `status --help`
  ran the kanban + PR/CI interlocks (gh canary trip, `daemon.log` write,
  WARN log lines in the "help" output), `wake --help` ran `autoup`, and
  `enable --help` exited 1 via the cron-guard. Every subcommand now carries
  its own help text (`SUBCOMMAND_HELP`); `cmd_autodown` scans the RAW
  subcommand argv for `--help`/`-h` (before `--json`/`--theme` stripping, so
  a help flag can never be swallowed as a flag value) and prints that text,
  exit 0, executing nothing. Non-help behaviour byte-identical.
- **`hscc project` help surface speaks `hscc project`, not `flightdeck`.**
  The project group rendered 209 help lines naming the retired standalone
  tool (`usage: flightdeck …` on every subcommand plus ~60
  `example: flightdeck …` epilogs whose project names were not even
  registered). The parser prog is now `hscc project`; every epilog is
  rewritten against real registry names (`hscc`, `ecofire-app`,
  `ecofire-bc`), with the canonical doubled form where the parse oracle
  demands it (`hscc project project new …`). `message read`/`broadcast`
  (dead since Telegram removal) are hidden from the help listing — handlers
  and tests intact — and `map-sessions`' unparseable
  `flightdeck map-sessions --json` example became
  `hscc project --json map-sessions`. Rendered path strings
  (`--registry`, `init --home`, `review --baseline`, self-update text) say
  "hscc-project home" instead of `~/.flightdeck`; the on-disk dir is
  unchanged (behaviour, not text). Pruned all 70 owner=F1 rules from
  `scripts/tests/cli_help_expected.json` — gate green.
- **`hscc cluster <subcommand> --help` executed the subcommand instead of
  printing help** (audit BROKEN B6 + B12, docs/audits/CLI_HELP_2026-10-15.md
  Class D). `_handle_cluster` handled `--help` only at GROUP level
  (`len(sys.argv) < 3 or sys.argv[2] == "--help"`), so every per-subcommand
  help request fell through to verb dispatch. Measured in a sandbox HOME with
  recording PATH canaries: `cluster stop --help` INVOKED the mutating
  `sparkrun stop --help` (B6 — the help token was consumed as the container id
  and forwarded), and `cluster status` / `hosts` / `info` / `jobs --help`
  shelled out to `sparkrun status` / `cluster list` / `cluster show hscc` /
  `cluster status` — read-only, but a help request that costs seconds and
  shells out is still executing something (B12). Only `monitor --help` was
  inert (it already had its own branch), and `up`/`down --help` refused via the
  F6 flag parser.
- **Fix:** the cluster group now carries a per-subcommand help table
  (`_CLUSTER_SUBCOMMAND_HELP`) and `_handle_cluster` intercepts `--help`/`-h`
  anywhere in the subcommand argv — before `--theme` stripping, before the
  engine load, before dispatch — printing that verb's usage and description,
  exit 0, executing nothing (the F6 `up`/`down` guard's shape, extended to the
  uncovered half). Each help line says whether the verb is read-only; `stop`'s
  says it stops a live container. Because the intercept scans the RAW argv,
  `cluster stop --id --help` prints help instead of stopping container `--id`,
  and `cluster stop --theme --help` can no longer swallow the help token as
  the palette name and dispatch the mutating verb with `--theme` as its
  container id. `status` / `hosts` / `jobs` / `info` / `stop --help` now exit
  0; `up`/`down --help` keep the F6 refusal contract byte-for-byte (rc=1 +
  "Nothing was started or stopped" — that message is quoted verbatim in
  another card's gate rules, so this card does not reword it). `monitor`'s
  help surface is operator-owned and untouched. Non-help behaviour
  byte-identical.
- **Engine-side second line of defence (`hscc-cluster/hscc.py` `cmd_stop`):**
  the engine now refuses a container id that is empty or flag-shaped
  (`--help`, `-h`, `--dry-run`, …) with a usage-carrying error instead of
  shelling `sparkrun stop <arg>` — B6's destructive shell-out stays closed
  even for callers that bypass the unified CLI (the back-compat standalone
  `hscc-cluster stop <id>` entry has no intercept in front of it). Same F6
  rule `up`/`down` apply to their flags: a destructive verb runs only on an
  argument that can actually name a container. A real container id is
  unaffected (byte-identical argv to sparkrun).
- Non-help behaviour unchanged, with one deliberate exception: the `cmd_stop`
  guard above, which turns the `stop ""` / `stop <flag>` paths from a
  sparkrun call into a refusal (that IS the fix). Group help, `monitor`'s
  help, the up/down F6 message, and every non-help verb path are untouched.
- **Importing the CLI executed the fleet** (audit BROKEN B11).
  `hscc_daemon/serving.py` resolved the cluster topology at IMPORT
  (module-level `resolve_cluster_config()`), so ANY invocation — every
  `--help`, even `hscc --help` in a fresh HOME — shelled
  `sparkrun cluster list --json` whenever `~/.hscc/cluster.json` was absent:
  help violated "help executes nothing", every CLI start paid seconds, and a
  fresh/CI machine shelled out implicitly. Topology resolution is now LAZY:
  `PRIMARY_NODE` / `ORCH_NODES` / `KEEPALIVE_NODES` / `VLLM_HEALTH_URL` /
  `VLLM_STOP_CMD` / `VLLM_START_CMD` / `VLLM_RECIPE` / `NAS_HOST` are PEP 562
  module attributes (the idiom `hscc-cluster/clusterlib.py` already uses) that
  resolve — with the unchanged cluster.json → sparkrun → documented-default
  precedence — on the first READ and cache for the process. Import + help
  execute nothing; any path that actually uses the topology gets exactly what
  it got before. `resolve_cluster_config()` stays public and eager-when-called,
  and the daemon loop resolves it explicitly at startup (where it always
  belongs), so daemon behaviour is unchanged.
- **Cluster group help overflowed the 80-column budget** (audit Class B,
  owner=F3 rows of docs/audits/CLI_HELP_2026-10-15.md). `hscc cluster --help`
  printed each subcommand entry as one hard line; the `monitor` entry (91
  cols) and the `up` entry (83 cols) were measured as overflow at width 80.
  The group listing now uses the two-line layout the template and per-verb
  surfaces already use: usage alone on its line, description wrapped with a
  fixed continuation indent (never col 0) at the same 78-col budget
  (`_CLUSTER_GROUP_ENTRIES` + `_print_cluster_group_help`). Entry wording is
  the base text verbatim — pinned by a canonical-whitespace test — and the
  operator-owned monitor surfaces (`_MONITOR_HELP`, `_parse_monitor_flags`,
  `cluster_live.py`, t_1cc33407) were not touched.
- **The F6 safety refusal was unreadable** (same audit rows): the refusal
  that `hscc cluster up/down --help` (or any unknown flag to a destructive
  verb) prints had two body sentences as single lines of ~90 and ~140 chars,

  wraps those sentences at the cluster help budget with a 2-space
  continuation indent; the dangling-`--theme` refusal from the same parser

  physical line breaks may move, words may not).
- **`hscc help cluster` overflowed at 80** (the COMMAND_HELP "cluster" value

- **`hscc template --help` wrapped without a continuation indent.** The
  `validate` and `apply` entries were single two-column lines (154 and 127

  `hscc help template`) lost its 111-column subcommand line — the verb list
  is short and each verb's flags now point at `hscc template --help`
  instead of being crammed into one overflowing row.
- **`hscc template preview|validate|apply --help` executed the verb and
  exited 1.** The help token was forwarded to the template engine as the
  template name, so `--help` printed `Template not found: --help` (and for
  `apply` reached the engine at all) and exited 1. `--help`/`-h` after a
  template verb now prints that verb's own usage and exits 0, before any
  engine import or dispatch; `hscc template -h` prints the group help like

- **`hscc api --help` and `hscc autodown --help` overflowed the help-surface
  gate at the mandated widths** (audit Class B, owner F4,
  docs/audits/CLI_HELP_2026-10-15.md). Both group HELP_TEXTs packed usage and
  description onto ONE hard line separated by a padding gutter, so the block

  width 80 plus 2 at width 120 (the `install-service` / `uninstall-service`

  fix that holds at every width; neither COLUMNS nor Rich can rescue a hard
  line here. Wording is the base's verbatim — re-flowed, never reworded.
- **`hscc api uninstall-service` embedded an absolute path in a hard
  sentence** (audit Class B, owner F4). The removal notice printed
  `no unit file at <absolute plist path> (nothing to remove)`, so with a long
  HOME root — the audit probes under a sandbox HOME — the line ran to 87+
  columns and overflowed at both mandated widths; Rich cannot wrap it either,
  because a filesystem path has no break opportunity. The path now gets its
  own indented line, rendered `~`-relative when it is under HOME (it always
  is, by construction of `api_launchd.API_PLIST_PATH`), and verbatim if
  anything ever rebinds that constant — so the notice is width-independent and
  still names exactly the file it acted on. This also shrinks the (D) surface:
  the path no longer leaks the sandbox/absolute HOME root into help-shaped
  output.
- **`hscc kanban blocked --help` / `hscc kanban stale --help` ran the verb**
  (audit BROKEN B10, Class D — folded into this card with operator approval,

  the GROUP's first token, so a per-subcommand help request fell through into
  the listing branch and enumerated every board: the autodown C3 interlock read
  logged WARN lines and wrote `~/.hscc/daemon.log` under the caller's HOME
  while "printing help" — and the mutating sibling of that same branch
  (`blocked --recover <id>`, `stale --archive <id>`) was one token away. Both

  `--help`/`-h` ANYWHERE in the raw argv — before `--json`/`--theme` stripping,

  seam. `stale` help is delegated to `kanban_cli` (its owner) rather than

  delegation says so instead of advertising a verb the build lacks. Non-help
  behaviour unchanged, `--recover`/`--archive` still dispatch normally.
- **`hscc heal-clear --help` EXECUTED the mutating verb** (audit BROKEN B4,

- **`hscc help heal-clear` / `hscc help heal-status` exited 1** (audit B5):

- **`hscc api <verb> --help` executed the verb instead of printing help**

- **CLI help-surface gate was interpreter-dependent (GATE-313).** The probe

  wide line means help CONTENT is width-aware and is reported as a new

  Re-baselined the 2 remaining A rules from the wide canonical form
  (`hscc --help` 2 → **1**, the collapsed pair was one logical line; `hscc

- **The rendered top-level help named the internal `flightdeck` package**

- **The main help spilled at 80 and 120 columns** (audit Class B: 10 bare

## [2.9.1] - 2026-10-15

### Added
- **`hscc cluster monitor --live`.** A refreshing fleet view. The host table has the same columns as `sparkrun cluster monitor` (Jobs, CPU/RAM/Swap/GPU %, temperatures, GPU power) without the per-container detail. Below it, one row per backend behind the proxy: node, port, model, the proxy aliases routed there, requests running and waiting, KV-cache use, and generation/prompt tokens per second (from each vLLM `/metrics`; rates appear from the second sample). A total row sums load per model. `--interval N` and `--cluster NAME` are accepted with `--live`; unknown flags are refused. Host metrics come from one long-running `sparkrun cluster monitor --json`, so SSH sessions are not reopened every tick. Plain `hscc cluster monitor` now prints one frame of the same view instead of a raw key/value dump. Narrow terminals (<110 cols) drop the routes and prompt-rate columns.
## [2.9.0] - 2026-10-15

### Added
- **`/v1/cluster/status` workloads now carry a `nodes` list.** Each entry of
  `workloads` gains one optional key, `"nodes": ["10.0.0.1", "10.0.0.2"]`,
  the host lines of that job's block in `sparkrun status` — the unit→node
  edge the iOS "Nodes & serving" screen needs. `cmd_cluster_status()`
  (`hscc-cluster/hscc.py`) already walked those lines and threw them away; it
  now keeps the IP for the `Job:` block in play. A TP=2 job legitimately
  reports BOTH nodes; a solo job reports its one. Purely additive — the
  existing four keys are untouched and byte-identical, no new subprocess
  call (the same `sparkrun status` output is already in hand), and `handle_cluster_status`
  forwards the workloads verbatim so the key rides through unchanged. Old
  clients keep decoding exactly as before; new clients must treat `nodes` as
  optional because a pre-field engine omits it.

### Changed
- **iOS operator console redesign (Phase 2).** One drawer shell with a single NavigationStack replaces the tab bar; chat is full-bleed; every list screen uses the same list recipe through Theme. Screens were merged or moved per the redesign spec (docs/design/IOS_REDESIGN_2026-10-14.md §5/§8): Fleet gains a read-only Models serving section, and Nodes & serving groups units by node via the new `nodes` field. New app icon ("Orbit"). A DEBUG-only capture harness (launch env vars, no taps) produces the light/dark screenshot set in docs/design/screens/. Fixed: the drawer glyph was blank because "serverrack" is not an SF Symbol. After pulling, run `cd ios-app && xcodegen generate`.

### Fixed
- **Every heal path could destroy the fleet it was protecting (2026-10-14 incident).** Six defects fixed together: a shared, durable heal lease so only one repair runs at a time (F2); auto-heal recreates ONLY the wedged unit — the old whole-template `--force-recreate` tore down healthy units mid-load (F3); proxy health now compares the LIVE router to actually-healthy units instead of trusting sparkrun's state-file PID, and repairs an orphan listener behind a cmdline vet (F4); a durable per-node heal circuit breaker stops a repair storm after 6 actions in 15 min, with `hscc heal-clear` (F5); `hscc cluster up/down` now REFUSES unknown flags (`--help` used to start the fleet) and `hscc start` detaches stdio (F6); and a launch guard refuses to start a vLLM on a host whose GPU already holds a workload outside the declared span — refuse + alert, never preempt, and 'status unavailable' is also a refusal (A2).
- **Dispatcher false 'GENUINE STALL' pages.** `kanban.max_in_progress` is a FLEET-WIDE cap, but the wedge detector computed roominess per board — with 3 tasks running across two boards a correctly-backlogged gateway was paged as wedged for an hour. Roominess now requires global headroom too, the healthy reason names which cap bound (`at_capacity (global)`), and recovery's gave-up latch clears when the stream is confirmed green (A1).
## [2.8.0] - 2026-10-14

### Added
- **`.githooks/commit-msg` strips attribution trailers** (`Co-Authored-By`,
  `Generated-By`, `Assisted-By`) from every commit message, in every clone and
  worktree (same `core.hooksPath` mechanism as the address guard). Agents were
  adding `Co-Authored-By: Hermes <hermes@nousresearch.com>`, which GitHub
  attributed to an unrelated account on this public repo.

### Fixed
- **iOS chat now receives the terminal REPL's replies.** The store-tail poller
  no longer waits for the `hermes serve` mount: it starts first, and a failed
  mount leaves the driver running tail-only instead of dead. With serve down
  and the project's REPL in tmux, a tail-only driver is mounted.
- **Orphaned `hermes serve` no longer 403s every mount.** On start, a serve
  already holding the port is adopted if it accepts the API's token; otherwise,
  if it is a `hermes serve` process, it is replaced. Foreign listeners are left
  alone. Failed mounts are retried at most once per 60s per project.
- **Correct transcript:** rows ordered by state.db id, compaction summaries
  shown as system rows (never as user messages), no duplicate user message for
  an app send, tool calls emit start and finish, persisted reasoning is shown.
- **iOS app:** the live banner reaches Connected (hello is matched by `type`),
  and the resume cursor rebases when the API restarts and renumbers events.
- **`scripts/api_smoke.py`:** end-to-end check that drives the real WebSocket
  protocol and fails unless the reply comes back in order.
## [2.7.0] - 2026-10-13

### Added
- **Every interactive chat the hscc CLI opens is now tmux-aware.** The iOS
  app delivers chat by typing into the project's REPL *pane*
  (`hscc-api/repl_inject`), so a chat started outside tmux was invisible to
  the phone — messages silently went to a hidden serve-hosted session.
  `hscc project chat` (and its `--resume` door) now goes through one shared
  helper, `flightdeck/core/tmux_chat.py`: inside tmux the chat opens in
  place as before; outside, it opens in (or attaches to) the named session
  `hscc-<project>`; when tmux is unusable (not installed, broken server, the
  named session runs another profile's REPL) it **stops and asks an explicit
  Y/N naming what is missing and the consequence — a silent non-tmux
  fallback never happens**, and non-interactive callers are refused, not
  surprised. The real tmux/ps/stdin seams carry the `repl_inject`-style
  identity guard (they refuse under pytest). `hscc-project/tests/test_tmux_chat.py`:
